title: Route Reopened
intent: Reopen a working port logistics corridor, keep two lifelines moving and preserve the hub records.
observed: The port has a useful river and bridge landmark, but repeated container stacks, very bright concrete bays and widely scattered tiny props dominate. The hub is represented by a tall tower and the water edge by a neat line of isolated rocks; the records destination is not visually obvious in these views.
camera: Frame the disrupted link and first relief movement, with the bridge as a secondary landmark. Give the hub entrance a closer view that is not dominated by the tower roof.
light: Keep the water/land distinction but reduce washed-out concrete. Check active source and Match lighting ownership for this port binding before tuning its exposure or fog.
ground: Make dockside slabs distinct from public sidewalk and service asphalt. Resolve gate and bridge approaches with continuous edging, flush crossings and road wear aligned to turning trucks. Improve the quay edge with a continuous foundation/water-contact treatment.
props: Group forklift/pallet/container activity at believable loading faces. Dress the hub doorway as a staffed routing office with a records cabinet or secured equipment room visible at tactical distance. Keep relief and Fuel bays visually different and traffic lanes open.
landscape: Replace the equally spaced river rocks with clustered bank or quay detail and restrained waterline staining; do not move bridge or navigable geometry.
